preamble: Affrication of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the postalveolar affricate [dʒ]: the large palatal contact is fronted and released with frication. Arabic jīm is the best-known case: Proto-Semitic *g had become palatal [ɟ] or [ɡʲ] by the time of the Quran and then [dʒ], the pronunciation of the Arabian Peninsula, Iraq and Modern Standard Arabic, while other dialects went on to [ʒ] or kept [ɟ].

examples.note: Hebrew gāmāl and Egyptian Arabic gamal keep the stop; South Levantine and most Maghrebi dialects continue to ʒamal.

sources: Watson, J. C. E. (2002). The Phonology and Morphology of Arabic. Oxford University Press. https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780199257591.001.0001
